response.summary: Overall, this notebook shows solid basic ML hygiene (stratified split and preprocessing kept inside a scikit-learn Pipeline), but there are two major issues that keep it in “review” status. The most important finding is that the data cleaning step converts non-matching date formats to missing values and then drops rows without reporting how many are removed, which could silently bias the dataset. Results are also not reproducible because the train/test split has no fixed random seed, and the reported test AUC changes noticeably between runs. In the interview, verify that she can (1) quantify and justify any row dropping/failed date parsing, (2) make evaluation reproducible (set seeds, use cross-validation), and (3) discuss threshold choice/recall trade-offs since the current 0.5 threshold yields very low recall.
